sarah (OrbitPay): Hey team — after a regional failover this morning our similarity search started returning nonsense. Known similar invoices now score ~0.0.

jordan (support): Ugh, sorry. Can you share the request_id from the response headers and which region you were targeting?

sarah (OrbitPay): request_id=rx-2024-06-18-0452, target_region=us-west-2

ops-bot: :warning: region-failover: 2024-06-18T04:52:03Z routed traffic us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 for customer orbitpay (3m12s). Fallback model served: redwood-embed-lite-384

sarah (OrbitPay): Example (sanitized):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, X-Region: us-west-2
Body: {"model":"redwood-embed-512","input":"Invoice #12345: payment due"}
```
Response headers showed: model=redwood-embed-lite-384

jordan (support): That would do it — your index expects 512-d vectors. Did you get exceptions from your NN library? Any retry loops?

sarah (OrbitPay): Yes — got shape mismatch errors, then some retries returned 384-d which caused mixed-dim failures. We also saw a billing spike from retries.

billing-bot: :money_with_wings: billing-alert: unusual retries & volume for orbitpay 04:52-04:56 UTC. Estimated +18% usage.

mike (runtime-eng): Quick triage: capacity shortage in eu-west-1 for 512-d embed pool. Smart router routed to standby region; fallback policy picked redwood-embed-lite-384 to preserve availability. That variant is lower-dim and incompatible with 512-d callers. Current policy favors availability over strict compatibility.

lina (ml-infra): We should never silently change embedding dimensionality. Options: (A) only fallback to compatible variants, (B) return an error and let client retry, or (C) serve a conversion shim (not ideal). We should prefer (A) or (B).

mike (runtime-eng): Agreed. I'll open a hotfix to make embedding fallbacks dimension-aware and to fail fast when no compatible variant is available.

jordan (support): Sarah — remedial plan: (1) roll your route back to the us-west-2 pool, (2) deploy fallback-policy hotfix so dims can't swap silently, (3) evaluate billing credit for retries. Can you run the repro after we flip routing?

sarah (OrbitPay): Repro steps we used:
```
# force region header to reproduce
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
 -H "X-Region: us-west-2" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-512","input":"test sentence"}' | jq .
```
I'll run after you confirm rollback.

mike (runtime-eng): Hotfix INF-7291 opened. Changing fallback: embeddings must match requested dim or return 425 (failed dependency). Rolling back routing for orbitpay now.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-patch INF-7291 to prod started by mike at 2024-06-18T05:01:12Z

lina (ml-infra): Adding server-side validation: if requested_dim != served_dim then emit metric + alert. Adding a canary test to catch this before rollback.

jordan (support): Sarah — we rolled back and applied the policy change. Please retry the curl and paste the response headers + embedding length if you can.

sarah (OrbitPay): Running now...

sarah (OrbitPay): Response: model=redwood-embed-512, embedding_length=512. No shape errors locally. Thanks for the quick turnaround!

jordan (support): Great. Filing a billing credit request for your retry spike and closing the immediate loop. Action items: mike to finalize hotfix & canary, lina to add dim-mismatch alert, billing to evaluate credit, support to notify when credits post.

mike (runtime-eng): Will follow up in INF-7291 and ensure failing-fast is default for embed-dim incompat.

billing-bot: credit-pending: orbitpay case CS-8821 — estimate under review.

jordan (support): Closing here — ping @support or reopen if anything else pops up :thumbsup:

sarah (OrbitPay): Thanks all, appreciate the quick help!
